title: Air Inlet Door Actuator
introduction:
The air inlet door selects outside air or recirculated cabin air. Its small reversible actuator moves the door, and a position sensor reports where the door is to the climate controller. It is the cabin’s air-source gatekeeper; the blower still moves the air, and the heater core and evaporator handle temperature.

I start with the right-hand lower instrument panel insulator shown in the first drawing. Removing that panel opens the working area; the next drawing identifies the actuator connector and mounting retainers. This guide covers removal and installation. It supplies no diagnostic test, calibration sequence or functional verification procedure.

items.name: Prevent unintended starting
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine. An accidental start may cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Remote start
items.detail: If equipped, disable remote start through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service requiring work underneath or around the vehicle. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, causing personal injury or death.

items.name: Eye and ear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Sharp edges
items.detail: Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to do so may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Climate control precautions
items.detail: Before beginning, review the supplied [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184), as required by the general safety reference. The actuator sequence involves the insulator, electrical connector and retainers; it calls for no refrigerant handling, heater-water-hose disconnection or electric booster heater servicing.

edits.text: Remove the retainers indicated along the upper edge of the RH (right-hand) lower instrument panel insulator, then remove the insulator.
edits.why: The highlighted panel is the access layer beneath the instrument panel. Removing it exposes the area used for the actuator work.

edits.text: Disconnect the air inlet door actuator connector highlighted in the next illustration. Remove the actuator’s mounting retainers shown in the inset, then remove the air inlet door actuator.
edits.why: The main view locates the electrical connection, while the inset separates the actuator’s mounting points from the surrounding hardware.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: position the air inlet door actuator and secure it with its retainers, reconnect the actuator connector, then refit the RH lower instrument panel insulator and secure its retainers.
edits.why: The actuator mounting and electrical connection are restored while the access area remains open; the insulator closes the area afterward.

changes.after: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine. An accidental start may cause serious personal injury.
